text:
maria: status dump from tonight's speculative bringup on ozma-mini-13b-q4_opt. ran the stochastic-speculative predictor (sampling-based fast-path) + deterministic verifier. overall token throughput ~2.1x and p50 latency ~1.7x better on our microbench. however, we see a ~2.2pt drop in ROUGE-L on the summarization holdout (summ-holdout-v4) and BERTScore-F1 ~1.1pt down.

kevin: thanks. sampling-based predictor — was it top-k or nucleus?

maria: top-k=40 with temp=0.6 for the predictor; verifier uses greedy. early_abort set to 0.08. speculative_sampler=true, fallback=beamlet(3). kv_prefetch on. quant profile q4_opt (mixed int8 kernels + fused attention).

anya: can you paste the exact eval run so I can reproduce?

maria: yep:

```
./eval_harness \
  --model=ozma-mini-13b-q4_opt \
  --speculative_mode=sampling \
  --spec_k=40 \
  --spec_temp=0.6 \
  --spec_fallback=beamlet:3 \
  --early_abort=0.08 \
  --kv_prefetch=true \
  --tasks=summarization,qa \
  --seed=2026 \
  --batch=16\
```

zach: what holdouts + metrics exactly?

maria: summarization: summ-holdout-v4 (1k examples), metrics: ROUGE-1/2/L + BERTScore-F1. QA: squad-like subset 500 ex, metrics EM/F1.

kevin: QA unchanged?

maria: QA EM and F1 within noise +/-0.3. summarization regression is concentrated on longer-document cases (>800 tokens).

anya: longer-doc bias makes sense. predictor sampling temp might favor short completions on quantized kernels. did you try lower temp or larger k?

maria: tried k=80 and temp=0.4 on a small sample: speedup dropped to ~1.7x but ROUGE-L improved to -0.6 vs baseline. so higher k/temp seems correlated with more regression.

zach: any signs of verifier hitting mismatch more often (i.e., verifier rejecting fast-path and doing full decode)? I want counts for speculative_accept_rate and extra_tokens_generated.

maria: yes, accept_rate ~72% for base config. when we increase k to 80 accept_rate drops to ~60% (so more verifier work). interestingly disabling kv_prefetch reduces accept_rate slightly but also reduces ROUGE delta.

ci-bot: benchmark job 7312224001 finished - logs: https://ci/internal/arty/7312224001 - artifacts: /artifacts/7312224001/metrics.json

kevin: can you push the experiment branch and the harness version? will run an fp16 baseline (no quant) and also try deterministic predictor (greedy) to compare.

maria: branch pushed: git@repo:redwood/exp/spec-ozma-q4opt-samp.git - tag spec-samp-2026-03-21. harness v2.4. uploaded summaries to /experiments/ozma-q4opt/spec-samp-2026-03-21/.

anya: next steps: (1) fp16 baseline vs q4_opt spec-sampling vs q4_opt spec-greedy; (2) paired bootstrap on ROUGE-L and BERTScore for significance; (3) extract the 50 most-regressed cases and run manual triage; (4) try a short-run with predictor warmed on the last 512 tokens of context to see if warm bias changes.

maria: doing paired bootstrap now for ROUGE-L (1k samples). preliminary p-value ~0.03. will post full CI numbers when ready.

zach: i'll take the qualitative triage tomorrow, focus on long-doc articles and see if there's truncation or incoherent last-paragraphs. tag me on the artifact when done.

kevin: if bootstrap holds, possible mitigation: increase verifier aggressiveness (lower early_abort), or prefer greedy predictor for long-docs via routing rule (if context_len>512 -> greedy spec). Could also fall back to fp16 for long-docs.

anya: add an ops metric to observe "speculative_length_bias" (avg length of fast-path completion vs final) and "accept_rate_by_context_len". we need per-bin stats.

maria: agreed. I'll add those to the metrics JSON and re-run nightly with new bins. will also run quick check with early_abort=0.04 to see tradeoffs.

ci-bot: scheduled job 7312231002 for paired-bootstrap (queued).

maria: thanks all. I'll consolidate numbers and open a follow-up thread with the 20 most-regressed examples and the proposed mitigations. :lab_coat:
